record.paper_title: Open problems on graph eigenvalues studied with AutoGraphiX
record.original_question: For every tricyclic graph G on n vertices with n = 20 or n at least 22, is the energy of G at most the energy of P_n^{6,6;6}, with equality only for P_n^{6,6;6}? Here P_n^{6,6;6} denotes the graph obtained from three copies of C6 and a path P(n−18) by adding a single edge from two of the 6-cycles to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from the third 6-cycle to the other endpoint.

evidence.page: Energy of a graph, HTML lines 1312-1319
evidence.quote: The problem of finding the tricyclic graphs maximizing the energy remains open... For n ≥ 22, we have a general conjecture obtained with AutoGraphiX. First let P_n^{6,6;6} denote the graph on n ≥ 20 obtained from three copies of C_6 and a path P_{n-18} by adding a single edge between each of two copies of C_6 to one endpoint of the path and a single edge from the third C_6 to the other endpoint of the P_{n-18}. Conjecture 5.11... Let G be a tricyclic graph on n vertices with n = 20 or n ≥ 22. Then E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6,6;6}) with equality if and only if G ≡ P_n^{6,6;6}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The energy of a simple graph G is defined as E(G) = sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. A connected graph on n vertices is called tricyclic if it has exactly n+2 edges (equivalently, its cycle space has dimension 3).

For each integer n ≥ 20, define the graph P_n^{6,6;6} as follows. Take three vertex-disjoint copies of the 6-cycle C_6, call them H_1, H_2, H_3, and a path P_{n-18} on n−18 vertices with endpoints u and v. Form P_n^{6,6;6} by adding one edge joining a vertex of H_1 to u, one edge joining a vertex of H_2 to u, and one edge joining a vertex of H_3 to v. (For n = 18 there is no path; for n = 19 the path consists of a single vertex.)

Prove or disprove the following: for every tricyclic graph G on n vertices, where n = 20 or n ≥ 22,
   E(G) ≤ E(P_n^{6,6;6}),
with equality if and only if G ≅ P_n^{6,6;6}.

status_evidence.title: On a Conjecture about Tricyclic Graphs with Maximal Energy
status_evidence.snippet: Li et al. proved the conjecture for connected bipartite tricyclic graphs on n ≥ 20 vertices with three vertex-disjoint cycles, apart from several small subclasses; the full conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress only; conjecture remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: The Maximal Matching Energy of Tricyclic Graphs (arXiv:1409.2038)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses tricyclic graphs and related extremal energy conjectures, citing the P_n^{6,6;6} conjecture as still standing.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to refer to the conjecture as open.
